input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: __aexit__ delegates to __exit__ with None for the exception type, value and traceback instead of forwarding the arguments it received
- failure path: an exception raised inside `async with attempt:` reaches __aexit__, which calls __exit__ with (None, None, None); __exit__ takes its success branch, records no failed outcome and returns None, so the exception propagates out of the async with and past the retry loop: the attempt is never recorded as failed and no retry happens

Reviewer finding
- description: __aexit__ ignores the received exc_type, exc_value and traceback and calls self.__exit__(None, None, None), so exceptions raised in the async with body are never passed on.
- rationale: Trigger: an exception is raised inside an `async with` attempt block. __aexit__ reports it as no exception, so the attempt is recorded as successful (set_result(None)) and no retry happens. The exception is not recorded for retry handling, so the retry loop never sees the failure. Fix: forward exc_type, exc_value and traceback to __exit__.
critique: The finding points to the same faulty operation: __aexit__ calls __exit__(None, None, None) instead of forwarding the exception arguments. The consequence is also the same: the failure goes unrecorded and no retry happens. Its claim that the attempt is recorded as successful is a minor variation and does not change the mechanism.
